lines.text: Flutter, tap, wiggle—who is moving in the leaves?
Catch the letter on the beat, then catch the tiny name.
Aphid appears—A found it. Aphid small in sight | legs, wings, or body make the clue feel right
B ... Bee; A bee is an insect with six legs; many bees visit flowers for nectar and pollen.
A tiny pause for C, then Cricket! It is an insect with long antennae; many males make chirping sounds by rubbing their wings.
under the garden leaves, Dragonfly belongs with D. A dragonfly is an insect with large eyes, two pairs of long wings, and an aquatic juvenile stage.
Question: E? Answer: Earwig. Earwig down low | tiny body clues help the name to show
Firefly appears—F found it. It is a beetle; many species produce light with special organs in the abdomen.
G ... Gnat; Gnat is a small fly with six legs, antennae, and one wing pair.
A tiny pause for H, then Hercules Beetle! It is a beetle; hard front wings cover softer flight wings.
